items.title: Cult of personality: What is Obiism? And who are ‘Obidients’? By Olu Fasan
items.description: Peter Obi is an enigma. A philosophy graduate, yet he is not a philosopher. A politician, yet he lacks the political skills to navigate the collegial world of politics. A presidential candidate, yet he hates the constraints of party politics, behaving as if he’s an independent candidate in a country that doesn’t permit independent candidacy. To Obi, his “movement”, “Obidients”, trumps any political party, yet “Obidient Movement” won’t be on the ballot. Obi is a celebrity politician who enjoys being hero-worshipped. His endorsement and even institutionalisation of his deification with the servile name “Obidients” – does he crave obsequiousness so much? – suggests he likes a cult of personality and believes he deserves an “ism” and a movement. But what is “Obiism”? And would “Obidients” transcend 2027 if Obi loses next year? First, what’s an ism? Well, it’s a doctrinal or philosophical term used as a shorthand for great ideas or to describe the beliefs of great leaders, and every ism has a movement. In Nigerian political history, two great leaders rightly earned an ism, and a movement. There was Zikism, the political philosophy of Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, and the Zikist Movement. There was also Awoism, Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s political and philosophical thoughts, and, of course, Awoists, followers of Chief Awolowo’s ideas and way of life. Today, 39 years after Awo’s passing in 1987, Awoism remains alive and there are die-hard Awoists flying the flag. But is Obi anywhere near as deserving of an ism and a movement as Dr Azikiwe and Chief Awolowo? Certainly not! Both Awolowo and Azikiwe were philosophers and intellectuals, who devoted enormous time to thinking and writing about human progress and nation building. Obi is by no stretch of the imagination a philosopher or even an intellectual, a weakness he himself exposes by identifying mainly as a businessman or a trader, but Socrates has different roles for philosophers and merchants. Awolowo and Azikiwe were also, in Plato’s characterisation, “philosopher-kings” who ran regional powerhouses as premier of the Eastern and Western regions, respectively, leaving enduring legacies. Obi’s claim of transforming Anambra State, as governor, is not so self-evident. Finally, Awo and Zik formed and nurtured viable political parties. Obi doesn’t believe in party formation; instead, he jumps from party to party, using political parties as mere special purpose vehicles! So, what’s Obi’s claim to an ism and a movement? A recent statement by his media office reads: “Today, the Peter Obi Media Office officially introduces him to Nigerians as the Candidate of Conscience. Calling a political leader a ‘candidate of conscience’ recognises an operational standard rooted in integrity, frugality and accountability.” According to the Obidient Movement’s website, there are 25,000+ registered Obidients, but there are hundreds of thousands on social media, and they all see in Obi the values of prudence, discipline and honesty. Compared to Bola Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar, Obidients view Obi as a saint. But genuine isms and movements are not based on personal qualities alone; they also need deeper political and philosophical thoughts and a track record of behaviours consistent with them. Yet, some of Obi’s behaviours have not been consistent with his widely perceived attributes. Take discipline and humility? Why does Obi enjoy drawing attention to himself even at the expense of decorum. I observed one incident in 2023 that has stuck with me. It was during a ceremony marking the anniversary of Governor Charles Soludo’s one year in office. Obi strolled in while the governor was delivering his speech. The hall erupted into a rapturous applause, with shouts of “Obi, Obi, Obi”! The governor momentarily stopped his speech. As Obi went to sit in the front row, nearly everyone in that row, including elderly and prominent Nigerians, stood to greet him. I wondered. Why did Obi, a supposed disciplined and humble man, come late to the event? Did he do it to test his popularity with Anambra people, a popularity already established with him winning nearly 90 per cent of the state’s votes in the just concluded presidential election? Did he do it to upstage the governor? Did he not realise how disrespectful it was to the governor to come in late the way he did and disrupt the event? How did he feel seeing those prominent and elderly Nigerians standing to greet him? In another event, a meeting of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Obi also strolled in late. Everyone in the front row, including Atiku, stood to greet him. He seemed to enjoy the public adulation. But that’s not discipline; that’s not humility. Obi may be humble personally, but politically he loves hero-worshipping. A President Obi won’t resist the allure of the office. Talking about the presidency, Obi’s strongest claim to the office is his much-trumpeted record as governor of Anambra State. I cannot question Obi’s achievements in Anambra, although it’s interesting that Governor Soludo, the current governor, is determined to repudiate, for political reasons, the legacy Obi claims in the state. For me, it’s utterly conceited for Obi to stake a claim to the presidency based on how he governed Anambra. Nigeria is not Anambra State, and experience has shown us that governing a state well is not an indication that someone would govern the country well. Some of those who voted for Tinubu in 2023 did so because they believed he transformed Lagos State as governor, and they wanted him to govern Nigeria the way he governed Lagos. But what have we seen? Some might retort that Obi is different from Tinubu. But I have shown, with the examples of his attitude to discipline and humility, that he’s not a saint. So, Nigerians must assess Obi’s suitability for the presidency not on his performance as Anambra State governor, but on his presidential campaign promises and the extent of their credibility and deliverability. Well, Obi’s agenda for 2027 is a subject for another day. But, as I wrote last week, regarding Atiku’s 12-point policy commitment, there’s a difference between the “poetry” of campaigning and the “prose” of governing. Thus, Nigerians must beware of empty soundbites. For instance, Obi’s mantra “from consumption to production” lacks analytical rigour. President Buhari had a similar mantra: “We will grow what we eat and eat what we grow.” But such soundbites are meaningless, and if they are based on the concept of import substitution, they are economically illiterate and damaging. As I said, Obi’s manifesto is a subject for another day; this piece is about his “ism” and the movement behind it. Which brings us to Obi and his Obidients’ approach to next year’s presidential election. From media reports, the Obidients are behaving as if Obi is running as an independent candidate. They formed a campaign group called Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement for Obi and his running mate, former Kano State governor Rabiu Kwankawso. But the OK Movement is operating completely detached from the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, the party sponsoring Obi and Kwankwaso for the election. Recently, the OK Movement unveiled a 59-member Presidential Campaign Council, but the NDC disowned it on the basis that only the party could form such a council. The DG of the OK Movement, John Ugulu, pushed back, arguing that the movement was independent and did not need the party’s approval to constitute the campaign council. But last week, the national head of operations of the OK Movement, Engr Francies Nnoli, resigned, saying it was wrong for the movement to operate independently from the NDC. Surely, all is not well between NDC and the OK Movement. As I wrote in a piece titled “2027: Why Seriake Dickson’s NDC can’t be a viable ruling party” (Vanguard June 25, 2026), Obi and Senator Dickson, NDC’s founder and leader, have divergent interests. Dickson recently declared on Arise TV: “I am not a Kwankwasiyya. I am not an Obidient. I am NDC.” But Obi’s fealty is to the Obidients, not NDC, which he’s merely “renting” for 2027. Yet, with such a divided house, the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket might fail. If it does, Obiism and Obidients will face wilderness years, the price of political hubris! The post Cult of personality: What is Obiism? And who are ‘Obidients’? By Olu Fasan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lack of planning
items.description: THE Prime Minister’s Committee on Civil Service Reforms has finalised its core recommendations, yet omitted any clear roadmap for the Planning Commission. The latter is routinely described as dysfunctional. Whether or not that description is true is beside the point. The more useful question is whether Pakistan will do what India did when its own planning body stopped delivering, or take a different course altogether. The two commissions began as near-twins. India’s was founded in 1950, Pakistan’s in 1953, both modelled on Soviet-style central planning and staffed by trained economists. Both were extra-constitutional bodies, created by executive order. Both were nominally chaired by the head of government and run day to day by a deputy chairman. Both produced Five-Year Plans as their central output and controlled how resources moved from the centre to the provinces or states. For roughly three decades, they were the same institution representing two flags. The split started in the late 1980s with a fork in the road that both countries reached and only one of them took. India hit its own balance-of-payments crisis in 1991. It liberalised, and it grew out of the crisis rather than falling into a cycle of dependency. Pakistan entered IMF structural adjustment in 1988 and never left. It is now on its 25th programme. That single divergence did more to determine the two institutions’ fates than anything that followed. Since 1988, IMF adjustment programmes have taken precedence over what became, in Pakistan, the largely academic exercise of five-year planning. The Commission became just another ministry, concerned mainly with approving projects, and constrained even there by a development budget whose size the finance ministry set. India’s Commission kept setting the fiscal and growth framework that the finance ministry worked within. Pakistan’s relationship has flipped: the framework now comes from Washington, and the Commission works around it. For a while, India’s Commission adapted. It absorbed the human development agenda from Mahbub ul Haq’s 1990 Human Development Report and embedded the eight National Missions of the 2008 National Action Plan on Climate Change into successive Five-Year Plans. It completed 12 plans across 65 years. But incremental change has a shelf life. By the early 2010s, India’s economy had become too large, too market-driven and too federally assertive for a centralised allocator to keep dictating terms to states that no longer needed its money. In 2014, the Modi government dissolved the Commission and replaced it with NITI Aayog, a leaner think tank with no power to allocate funds, built around advisory strategy, SDG tracking and competition between states. The point is not that India dissolved a failing institution. It dissolved a working one, because a model built for 1950 was not fit for 2015. The civil service reform committee has left out crucial reform for planning institutions. Pakistan never reached that fork, because it never adapted enough to outgrow the old model in the first place. Where India’s Commission built capacity and then had to be redesigned, Pakistan’s mostly stood still. The 18th Amendment in 2010 devolved 17 ministries to the provinces. But nobody redesigned what the federal Planning Commission should do once the subjects it used to plan for no longer belonged to it. It was recast into a full ministry in 2013-14, gaining nominal breadth, Vision documents, SDG coordination, CPEC planning, and losing whatever independence it once had. Four provincial planning and development departments expanded around it, each building its own project pipeline — and national development spending across federal and provincial channels now exceeds Rs3.5 trillion. The PSDP, the Commission’s one remaining function, amounts to just seven per cent of the federal budget, its ceiling fixed by the Finance Division, the IMF interlocutor. This is where the comparison stops. NITI Aayog, for all its own gaps, has a claim: a 165pc increase in renewable capacity in a decade, an NDC (Nationally Determined Contributions) process it coordinated across ministries and industry, and the world’s first government-led subnational SDG index, lifting India’s national SDG score from 58 to 71 between 2018 and 2024 by making states compete on published rankings. It has real failures too. But it measures them. It tracks 113 indicators across every state and publishes the results. Pakistan has no institution that does either job for its own provinces. Nobody ranks them on outcomes. Nobody has evaluated whether the PSDP, after decades and trillions of rupees, has achieved what it was funded to achieve. If we count what’s missing, nine separate failures emerge: a macro framework that has surrendered to the IMF since 1988; a series of launched and abandoned Vision documents; a collapse in human development that has left Pakistan’s HDI ranking 20 places behind India’s, with Bangladesh ahead of both; a PSDP process captured by political patronage rather than sustainable development logic; a think-tank function that atrophied while Mahbub ul Haq’s own institutional descendants scattered abroad; a climate and environmental blindspot in a country that ranks among the 10 most climate-vulnerable states; a federal role left undefined after the 18th Amendment; no subnational monitoring or evaluation framework; and, binding all of it together, an institution that has expanded in size while abandoning its function, producing the appearance of planning where substance no longer exists. Put together, this is not one failure of implementation. It is three failures of obsolescence, layered on top of each other: 1) globally, the development agenda moved from GDP and infrastructure towards human capabilities, the SDGs and climate finance, and the Commission never followed, 2) domestically, four periods of military rule and an un-redesigned federal mandate after 2010 did separate, serious damage, and 3) functionally, what remains is a gatekeeping exercise inside a PSDP ceiling set in Washington, approving a backlog of projects, the so-called throwforward, worth several trillion rupees more than can ever be funded. Pakistan does not lack planning institutions. It lacks a plan for its planning institutions. That is the reform the PM’s committee left out, and the one that was never optional. The writer is a climate expert. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

Dangerous border
items.description: WITH no let-up in terrorist attacks on Pakistan by elements finding refuge in Afghanistan, Islamabad has again launched kinetic action in the border area to target terrorist groups. The actions have resulted in exchanges of fire with the Afghan Taliban regime. Pakistan seems to be trapped in a cycle of escalation for the simple reason that Kabul is unwilling to act against terrorist groups active on its soil, such as the banned TTP, that seek to harm this country. Until this fundamental issue is addressed, bilateral ties will not improve. It was reported on Wednesday that the military had shot down drones apparently originating from Afghanistan as they attempted to violate Pakistani airspace. Earlier, Pakistan had launched air strikes in the border area, which killed a number of terrorists, after a spate of violent attacks, including the assault targeting the old Police Lines in Kohat last week. Pakistani forces also thwarted infiltration attempts in the Kurram area, which resulted in an exchange of fire with the Afghan Taliban. Along with taking kinetic action, Pakistan has highlighted this grim situation on the world stage. The UN Security Council has condemned the Kohat terrorist attack, calling for the “perpetrators … and sponsors” of the atrocity to be brought to justice. Pakistan had earlier told the UNSC that it would respond to threats originating from Afghanistan in self-defence. Moreover, the deputy prime minister, while speaking at a meeting of the OIC contact group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the ongoing UN General Assembly session, reiterated the need for a verifiable mechanism to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism. China, as well as Muslim states such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar, has backed diplomatic efforts to resolve the differences between Kabul and Islamabad. While hostilities are undesirable, if the Afghan Taliban take no action against those who spill innocent blood in this country, Pakistan will have no option but to take action to defend itself against terrorism. Yet while immediate threats must be confronted, long-term peace can only come through dialogue, and a commitment by the Taliban to curb cross-border terrorism. As has been highlighted in these columns previously, a bevy of terrorist groups call Afghanistan home, and pose a threat to the whole region, not just Pakistan — although this country, owing to its physical proximity, has been hit the hardest. Therefore, only a sustained and coordinated regional effort can succeed in eliminating the terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan. It is clear that, ultimately, the Taliban must decide whether they want to integrate with the rest of the region, or remain a pariah regime because of their stubborn ideological attachment to their violent comrades. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

items.title: You seek sanctuary against kidnappers – Baffour Awuah defends retreat to Parliament
items.description: Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah has defended his decision to retreat to Parliament after an encounter with officials from the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). The lawyer said he believed he was facing an unlawful arrest and feared he could be abducted. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, Baffour Awuah said an EOCO official approached him after he had addressed the media outside court. “She firmly held my wrist, with the greatest of respect,” he said. According to him, he agreed to go to EOCO but insisted on travelling in his own vehicle. “I told her that, look, if you need me at EOCO, I will join you. Let’s go. I’m coming in my car,” he said, adding that the official refused and insisted that he travel in the EOCO vehicle. Baffour Awuah said he then asked the official to identify herself and prove that she was from EOCO. “It was at that point that I asked her, Where is your ID? What even shows you are from EOCO? She couldn’t even produce it,” he said. The MP said the encounter raised fears for his safety. “Then I thought that, look, this is one of the kidnappings that have been going on, illegal; this is one of the kidnappings, state-sponsored kidnappings that have been going on, and so I will not sit in the car,” he said. He said he instead decided to remain in his vehicle and go to EOCO when he was satisfied that the process was proper. “I will not sit in the car. So I would rather sit in my car and now make sure that when EOCO is right ready to do the right thing, I will go there,” he said. Baffour Awuah also rejected suggestions that he was running away when he went to Parliament. “This is an unlawful arrest,” he said. “This is an unlawful arrest. An attempt to abduct me by persons who don’t want to work with law, and so it is not wrong if I’m seeking sanctuary.” He defended his decision to seek protection at Parliament despite the House being on recess. “It is not wrong if I’m seeking sanctuary. In fact, you seek sanctuary against kidnappers, and so if I’m seeking sanctuary, it is not wrong. My brother, is it wrong?” he asked. Baffour Awuah maintained that he was not afraid of appearing before EOCO when the proper process was followed. “I’m not afraid of anything,” he said. He also insisted that his work as a lawyer did not justify his arrest. “Which lawyer has gotten which lawyer, I mean, just by you representing your client, right? You are arrested for representing it doesn’t happen,” he said. He added that he was prepared to face EOCO when it was ready to follow the proper process. “And so, you know, when they are ready to do the right thing, I will go. They have not invited my person, and I’ve established that.”

items.title: Législatives 2026 : le PAM en tête avec 97 sièges
items.description: Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Abdelouafi Laftit, a communiqué les premiers résultats officiels (non encore définitifs) des législatives du 23 septembre 2026. Avec 97 sièges remportés, le Parti de l'Authenticité et de la Modernité (PAM) s'impose en tête de ce scrutin. Le Parti du tracteur est suivi du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) avec 66 sièges, du parti de l'Istiqlal (65 sièges), du parti de la justice et du développement (PJD) avec 54 sièges, le Mouvement populaire (MP) 29 sièges, l'Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) 26 sièges, le parti du Progrès et du Socialisme (PPS) 19 sièges, l'Union constitutionnelle (UC) 17 sièges, la Fédération de gauche (8 sièges) à égalité parfaite avec le Mouvement Démocratique et Social (MDS), qui décroche également 8 sièges au niveau des circonscriptions électorales, a indiqué le ministre. Pour leur part, le Front des Forces Démocratiques (FFD) et le Parti de l'Équité (Insaf) s'adjugent chacun 2 sièges au sein de la future assemblée. Enfin, le Parti des Nouveaux Démocrates (PND) et le Parti de l'Unité et de la Démocratie (PUD) ferment la marche en obtenant chacun 1 siège. A cette occasion, le ministre a rappelé que quelque 3.006 observateurs ont été associés à cette opération, dont 730 du Conseil national des droits de l'Homme (CNDH), et 200 étrangers, témoignant ainsi de l'ouverture de l'expérience marocaine sur son environnement. Le 23 septembre a connu la participation d'environ 6 millions d'électeurs et électrices sur 15,8 millions d'inscrits sur les listes électorales, a indiqué Abdelouafi Laftit avec un taux de participation de 38,02%. Il a déclaré que l'affluence des citoyens aux urnes « a été forte, comme à l'accoutumée dans les provinces du Sud » , où ce taux a atteint 77% dans la région de Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra, 53,48% dans la région de Guelmim-Oued Noun, et 61% dans la région de Dakhla-Oued Ed-Dahab. « Cela constitue la meilleure preuve de l'attachement des citoyens de ces provinces chéries à leur marocanité et de leur implication effective dans les différentes institutions représentatives », a affirmé le ministre. Laftit a décrit la campagne électorale, notamment dans son volet médiatique comme « intense » sur le terrain, à travers les initiatives de communication menées par les instances politiques, qui ont frôlé les 21 000 initiatives de communication, attirant environ 1 million et demi de participants, soit une moyenne de 115 000 participants par jour. « Ce sont des chiffres qui n'avaient été enregistrés lors d'aucun des scrutins précédents » , a indiqué le ministre de l'Intérieur, soulignant que les tournées sur le terrain ont constitué le mécanisme le plus utilisé par les candidats, attirant environ 730 000 participants, suivies par les meetings politiques avec près de 407 000 participants. « Il est certain que ces données montrent que les partis politiques ont déployé de grands efforts pour exposer leurs programmes et convaincre les électeurs » , en utilisant divers moyens tels que la distribution de tracts et la tenue de réunions, tout en ayant recours aux espaces médiatiques écrits et électroniques ainsi qu'aux plateformes de communication numérique, a ajouté le même intervenant. Par ailleurs, Laftit a ajouté que les infractions et plaintes enregistrées au cours de cette étape ont été traitées conformément à la loi, et celles comportant des soupçons d'actes illégaux ont été déférées aux autorités compétentes, sans que les cas isolés enregistrés n'aient d'impact sur le déroulement général de la campagne électorale ou ne portent atteinte à l'intégrité de l'ensemble du processus électoral. The post Législatives 2026 : le PAM en tête avec 97 sièges appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: AJK Legisla­tive Assembly to elect new president today
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The AJK Legisla­tive Assembly will meet on Thurs­day to elect the region’s new president for a five-year term, a process that has remained pending since January following the death of inc­umbent Barrister Sultan Mahmood. Dr Najeeb Naqi of the ruling PML-N and Chaudhry Latif Akbar of the PPP are contesting the election. Both are senior parliamentarians who have held key positions in successive governments of their respective parties. Under the AJK Consti­tution, the president is elected by the members of the Legislative Asse­mbly by a majority of the total membership. The PML-N has 31 lawmakers, excluding Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, against 14 of the PPP, in the 46-member Hou­­se. Meanwhile, the AJK Election Com­mission also announced the schedule for election to four seats of the AJK Council, whose five-year terms expired last month. Polling will be held on Oct 12 from 10am to 1pm, with coun­ting to begin immediately after polling. According to the schedule, nomination pap­ers will be received on Oct 1 between 9am and 2pm. Scrutiny will be held at 10am on Oct 2. Appeals against rejection of nomination papers may be filed on Oct 5 between 9am and 12:30pm. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

items.title: Hasta luego, Maricarmen
items.description: Ayer, 23 de septiembre de 2026, 50 policías antidisturbios arrancaron a Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, de la casa del acomodado distrito madrileño de Retiro en la que llevaba viviendo casi toda su vida. Cumplían la orden de desahucio lograda por la nueva propiedad del inmueble, que pretendía subirle el alquiler de 500 a 2.650 euros mensuales. Para lograrlo, habían sacado antes a porrazos y ráfagas de gas lacrimógeno a los cientos de personas, algunas muy notorias, que habían acudido al alzamiento para intentar evitarlo. Confieso que, mientras asistía hipnotizada a la retransmisión minuto a minuto que hicieron los medios de esta especie de David-Maricarmen contra el Goliat de la especulación inmobiliaria, me debatía entre la indignación, la vergüenza y, sí, cierto sentimiento de hipocresía personal y colectiva. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dirigentes del PSOE lamentan las “contradicciones” de Zapatero con las joyas: “¿Dónde queda la ética?”
items.description: Las joyas de José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero se le siguen atragantando al PSOE. Las explicaciones del expresidente del Gobierno sobre el origen del ajuar, un “obsequio” de Arabia Saudí en 2007 que guardaba en una caja fuerte en su despacho, han dejado a los socialistas más allá de Ferraz “igual o más” alicaídos de lo que ya estaban por la causa judicial que afecta a uno de sus grandes referentes. Lejos de contentarlos, han contribuido al desconcierto y enojo. “Cuesta digerirlo, porque encima que llegan tarde resulta que [las joyas] fueron el regalo de una monarquía medieval de un país que no respeta los derechos humanos, donde por ejemplo ser homosexual es un delito que se castiga con la muerte. A mí eso no me vale. ¡Cuando nosotros somos los del matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo o que defiende la igualdad entre hombres y mujeres!“, lamenta un secretario general autonómico. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El valor de las joyas de Zapatero según la tasación pericial apunta a un delito fiscal, aunque haya prescrito
items.description: José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero ha explicado, más de cuatro meses después del hallazgo de las joyas durante el registro policial de su despacho de la calle Ferraz y transcurridos casi tres meses del plazo que él mismo se dio ante el juez José Luis Calama, cuál es su origen. El conjunto de piezas, que incluyen rubíes, esmeraldas y zafiros y que un informe pericial encargado a Ansorena valoró en 1,3 millones de euros, fue, según el expresidente, “un obsequio realizado como atención personal" por el entonces rey de Arabia Saudí, Abdalá Bin Abdulaziz al Saud, quien se lo entregó en Madrid, en la vivienda familiar ubicada en el Palacio de La Moncloa en junio de 2007, cuando era jefe del Ejecutivo. Lo que sigue son las implicaciones legales y éticas de esas explicaciones enviadas al magistrado de la Audiencia Nacional con el propósito de enterrar la pieza separada sobre las joyas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ariana Harwicz, escritora excluida del Cultur Alh: “En la cultura se justifica la cancelación a los judíos”
items.description: Ariana Harwicz (Buenos Aires, 48 años) se ha visto envuelta en un torbellino desde que el viernes pasado anunció en redes sociales que había sido desinvitada unos días antes de que arrancara el Festival Cultur Alh de Granada que se celebra hasta el domingo en la ciudad andaluza. Ha habido una carta de rechazo a su exclusión por parte de la Universidad y otra de siete escritores invitados al festival que mostraban su acuerdo con la decisión. Este miércoles, más de 350 autores, críticos, pensadores, libreros y gestores culturales han mostrado su apoyo con la argentina y el escritor irlandés John Banville ha anunciado que no acudirá al festival de Granada como estaba previsto. Harwicz responde al teléfono desde su casa en Francia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El último acto de lealtad de ‘Lur’, el perro que delató al asesino de su dueño gracias a que tenía chip
items.description: El día era soleado y caluroso e invitaba a un baño en el pantano de Yesa, en Zaragoza, y una excursión por sus alrededores. Eso pensaron decenas de bañistas que se encontraban allí el 4 de agosto y también una familia que decidió dar un paseo. Cuando estaban cerca de una antigua fábrica abandonada, la ruta se vio interrumpida por un hallazgo escabroso . Observaron lo que parecían unos restos humanos en la orilla de una de las playas que se han formado de forma natural en algunos puntos del embalse. Nueve partes del cuerpo de un hombre adulto con barba blanca. ¿Quién era? ¿Cómo había acabado allí? ¿Cuánto tiempo llevaba en ese pantano? Todas las respuestas se responderían después, gracias al perro Lur . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Raúl Arévalo: “He trabajado con algún director que hoy sería denunciado. Seguro que ahora no se comportaría así”
items.description: El abuelo de Raúl Arévalo (46 años, Madrid) solo llegó a bañarse una vez en el mar. Se llamaba Víctor, era hortelano y pasó su vida en un pueblo de Segovia, Martín Muñoz de las Posadas. “Mira qué friki , esta es la única vez que fue a la playa en Benidorm. Se remangó para ver cómo era eso de bañarse”, explica el actor y director madrileño. En la pantalla de su ordenador, enseña una fotografía: un hombre mayor, aferrado a su cayado y vestido con capas y capas, sumerge los pies en el agua ante la atónita mirada del resto de bañistas. De aquella imagen le separan unas décadas y, al mismo tiempo, un mundo. Pero sin embargo, hace poco le inundó una sensación que cree muy similar a la que tuvo que experimentar entonces su abuelo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los hombres que caminan por delante de sus parejas: por qué esos pasos por delante sí importan
items.description: En TikTok, la red social que se erige como el espejo digital que mejor refleja comportamientos y tendencias, existe ya un paraguas temático bajo el que se encuadran vídeos que plasman la costumbre que algunos hombres tienen de andar siempre varios pasos -o incluso metros- por delante de sus parejas. “Un buen marido camina a tu lado”, titula Allan Ripp a una columna publicada en Wall Street Journal . “Mi mujer se quejaba de que yo tendía a caminar unos pasos por delante de ella, así que cambié mi forma de actuar”, asegura. Porque acompasar el ritmo al de la pareja a la hora de andar significa mucho más de lo que a priori pudiera parecer. La manera en que las personas caminan juntas, quién va delante, quién va detrás y si alguien se da cuenta de ello puede mostrar con sutileza el poder, la cercanía emocional y la atención existentes dentro de una relación. Las investigaciones en psicología social señalan que habitualmente, la posición física de las personas es un reflejo de los roles psicológicos que desempeñan. Un estudio publicado en el Journal of Nonverbal Behavior reveló que quienes tienden a caminar por delante son más proclives a ser percibidos como líderes o como controlan la interacción. ¿Es esto necesariamente negativo? En absoluto, pero el Dr. John Gottman, especializado en relaciones de pareja, asegura en sus investigaciones que la conexión emocional se manifiesta en pequeños gestos. Por descontado, adaptar el ritmo a los demás a la hora de caminar es uno de ellos y cuando una pareja no responde a las pequeñas señales cotidianas del otro, la distancia emocional crece. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los ‘ricos’, según Irene Montero
items.description: Irene Montero ha lanzado su candidatura hablando de los ricos y la acaparación de riqueza . Podemos está rascando en el fondo del barril porque sus medidas parecen ya unicornios: poner el salario mínimo en 1.800 euros por 30 horas a la semana o bajar los alquileres un 40% por decreto. El populismo de izquierdas ya no genera los mismos efectos que en el 15-M. Y, sin embargo, el problema que tienen hoy las clases medias y trabajadoras en España no son los superricos o los multimillonarios, sino una cuestión de escasez en el día a día. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una sesión del Congreso ‘incendiada’ por el gas pimienta: de las bromas por “el ataque híbrido” al riesgo de sanciones al PP
items.description: Un espray de gas pimienta alteró ayer la sesión parlamentaria en el Congreso. El aerosol no fue introducido por ningún elemento ajeno a las Cortes ni lo lanzó ningún manifestante desde la calle: la diputada del PP, Ana Vázquez Blanco, había comunicado a su grupo el día anterior su decisión de exhibirlo durante la sesión de control al Gobierno para denunciar así la inseguridad en las calles de Ceuta. En principio, dicen fuentes populares, todos pensaron que lo llevaría vacío pero el gas se propagó por algunos conductos del Congreso. La policía del Cámara baja logró hacerse con el “arma” de la discordia a las 12.45, después de más de tres horas de especulaciones y pesquisas para aclarar por qué el tóxico provocó que 12 personas tuvieran que ser atendidas por los servicios médicos y se precintaran espacios de dos edificios a ambos lados de la carrera de San Jerónimo. “La película que se montan estos socialistas”, se justificaba después de todo en televisión la diputada, que es una habitual tertuliana. Además, es policía de profesión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Exteriores pide a los consulados “información diferenciada” de los nacionalizados por la ‘ley de nietos’ que acreditaron ser descendientes de exiliados
items.description: El Ministerio de Exteriores ha enviado a las oficinas consulares de todo el mundo las instrucciones que deberán seguir para cumplir con la decisión del Tribunal Supremo de suspender el derecho al voto de los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos . El documento les pide que remitan a la Oficina del Censo Electoral la “información” de las personas que hayan obtenido la nacionalidad española mediante el procedimiento establecido en la ley de Memoria Democrática de 2022. items.title: La justicia como “contrapoder de Estado”
items.description: Hay días en que las decisiones judiciales nos recuerdan algunos ejercicios de prestidigitación. Nada por aquí, nada por allá, pero resulta que había —o alguien ha creído ver— un elefante en la habitación. O al revés. Allá donde parecía existir una grave responsabilidad por inacción o falta de diligencia frente a una catástrofe natural, por ejemplo, solo hay el fondo vacío de una chistera. En algún momento se recuperarán la calma y los esquemas clásicos en la distribución del poder, también con respecto a las salas de justicia, pero por ahora es desde ellas desde donde emergen decisiones que marcan la vida política del país. A veces, para desconcierto y perplejidad general. El papel de los tribunales en el control de las decisiones del ejecutivo y el legislativo ha adquirido tanta relevancia que no faltará quien proponga que se deje de utilizar la expresión poder judicial para empezar a hablar de la justicia como “contrapoder de Estado”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Giro de guion en la muerte en Baqueira del arquitecto de la burguesía catalana
items.description: El mes de diciembre acabó con los círculos económicos y empresariales de Barcelona vestidos de luto. Carles Vilarrubí , esposo de Sol Daurella, la presidenta de Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, falleció a los 71 años de edad y su velatorio , el 29 de diciembre, congregó en el tanatorio de Sant Gervasi a todos aquellos que querían despedirse de quien fue, entre otras dedicaciones, directivo del Barça, impulsor de Catalunya Ràdio y chófer de la confianza de Jordi Pujol . En otra planta del mismo tanatorio, situado en la parte alta de la ciudad, se instaló ese mismo día el velatorio de Josep Juanpere Miret, el arquitecto que diseñó las sedes de varias de las grandes empresas que operan en Cataluña y que, durante años, se especializó en el interiorismo de establecimientos de lujo como el Hotel Arts, el Grand Marina, el The Mirror, el Hesperia Tower, todos ellos en Barcelona, el Kimpton Los Monteros, en Marbella, o los exclusivos apartamentos de Alcántara 25, en Madrid. Juanpere había fallecido súbitamente en su apartamento de Baqueira (Vall d’Aran) por lo que parecieron causas naturales. Este miércoles trascendió la detención de su mujer por, supuestamente, haber causado la muerte de forma intencionada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Quebrantar una orden de alejamiento con un ‘me gusta’, una perdida o un WhatsApp borrado: así hostigan a sus exparejas los agresores machistas
items.description: Enviar un mensaje por WhatsApp, aunque el mensaje sea tan solo un punto, puede ser delito si hay en vigor una prohibición de comunicación por violencia de género. “He tenido casos en los que le ha mandado un punto, una letra, le ha hecho una llamada perdida y lo condenamos por quebrantamiento”, afirma rotunda la jueza María Auxiliadora Díaz. ¿Pero ver una historia de Instagram? ¿Darle me gusta a una publicación? ¿Transferir unos céntimos por Bizum? Son ejemplos de cómo los agresores van encontrando en las innumerables plataformas digitales nuevos canales para hostigar a sus exparejas y la Justicia va detrás, sentando jurisprudencia sobre qué supone un quebrantamiento ―penado con entre seis meses y un año de cárcel― para evitar que se repita. En la última memoria de la Fiscalía General del Estado 2026 , publicada hace dos semanas, se destaca cómo se ha consolidado que los tribunales acepten el rastro de un mensaje eliminado como suficiente para acreditar el quebrantamiento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Puede una IA desenmascarar a otra? Pangram, una herramienta casi infalible para detectar textos y novelas creadas por máquinas
items.description: El libro C’était ça ou mourir ha recibido el premio de novela Fnac, el Medusa y algún otro, lleva más de 35.000 ejemplares vendidos y está entre los candidatos a los grandes galardones del otoño literario. Desde este miércoles, el libro tiene otro mérito: es el primer gran escándalo francés de literatura presuntamente hecha con inteligencia artificial (IA). Su autor, el canadiense de origen haitiano Thélyson Orélien, lo niega. Dice que acabó el primer borrador en 2019 (ChatGPT salió a finales de 2022) y que su tradición literaria “haitiana y caribeña” puede haber causado confusión porque “las imágenes, las repeticiones y el ritmo transmiten una palabra viva”, ha explicado en medios franceses. Su editorial, Grasset, de momento le apoya . La denuncia contra Orélien surgió de una cuenta anónima en X. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las ‘kellys’ reclaman la jubilación anticipada: “Tengo 63 años. Hacer camas en un hotel de cinco estrellas es un matadero”
items.description: María Ibáñez (nombre ficticio) nació hace 63 años en Colombia y lleva 30 residiendo en España, donde ha trabajado los últimos 25 como camarera de piso en Madrid. Dice que le gustaría prejubilarse por la cantidad de enfermedades musculoesqueléticas que arrastra , pero que ni su limitada carrera de cotización ni su precaria posición económica se lo permiten. “Hacer camas en un hotel de lujo es un matadero”, enfatiza con respecto al establecimiento de cinco estrellas en el que ahora mismo trabaja. “Hay mucha presión. Los clientes son de mucho nivel, pagan un precio muy alto por la habitación y quieren encontrarlo todo perfecto. Si una camarera de piso puede hacer hasta 20 camas en un turno diario en un hotel medio, yo no hago más de ocho habitaciones, pero es que la limpieza de cada una de ellas me puede llevar 40 minutos”. Ibáñez se queja especialmente del trato de las mutuas de trabajo . “No constatan ninguna de mis enfermedades porque para ellos no son fruto del trabajo o del esfuerzo que hago en el día a día, sino que las catalogan como enfermedades comunes. Solo establecen que una persona está mal y que puede cogerse una baja cuando tiene un brazo o una pierna rota”. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) ha duplicado sus escaños en las tres elecciones regionales alemanas que se han celebrado este septiembre . La extrema derecha alemana venció en las urnas en el Estado de Sajonia-Anhalt, donde tiene la opción de gobernar por primera vez desde la caída del nazismo. En otro land del Este del país, Mecklemburgo-Pomerania Occidental, ganó los comicios del pasado domingo con un 38% de los votos. Y en Berlín, la capital, quedó tercera pero subiendo de 17 a 29 escaños en su Parlamento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Lapili: “Cuando dicen que promuevo la obesidad: solo estoy existiendo y viviendo”
items.description: Cuando Pilar Robles, Lapili (Ciudad Real, 32 años) llegó a Madrid hace diez años ya tenía una tribu: otros jóvenes bailarines adoradores de los ritmos callejeros jamaicanos y caribeños a los que había conocido gracias a la magia de las redes sociales y con los que quedaba en los bajos de Azca a bailar. “¿Ves esas cristaleras? Funcionan como espejos y por eso nos encantaba ponernos delante”, explica exactamente ahí esta creadora multidisciplinar (de hecho, es también artista textil), que pensó que su vocación estaba en la moda hasta que se atrevió a intentar una carrera como cantante. Ahora es un nombre consolidado en una escena, el dancehall , en la que el canon del pop vuela por los aires. El primer adelanto de su nuevo disco, Badda, es una bomba, pero un día antes de irse a Nueva York por una colaboración que no puede revelar, adelanta que quedan muchos cartuchos por explotar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: This is an unlawful arrest – Baffour Awuah defends flight from EOCO officers
items.description: Lawyer and Manhyia South MP, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, has described an attempt by officials of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) to take him into custody as an “unlawful arrest.” Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, Mr Baffour Awuah said an EOCO official approached him after he had addressed the media outside court and told him he was needed at the agency. He said the official then held his wrist firmly, forcing him to wriggle himself free. “She held my hand so tight, so firmly that I had to wriggle myself from her hand,” he said. According to him, he offered to drive himself to EOCO, but the official insisted that he could not use his own vehicle. He said he subsequently asked to see identification proving the officers were from EOCO, but the request was denied. “It was at that point that I asked her, Where is your ID? What even shows you are from EOCO? She couldn’t even produce it,” he said. Mr Baffour Awuah said the circumstances made him suspect that the incident could be linked to the kidnappings he alleged had been occurring. “I thought that, look, this is one of the kidnappings that have been going on, illegal; this is one of the kidnappings, state-sponsored kidnappings that have been going on, and so I will not sit in the car,” he said. He maintained that he was prepared to cooperate with EOCO if the agency followed what he described as the proper process. “I would rather sit in my car and now make sure that when EOCO is right ready to do the right thing, I will go there. I’m not afraid of anything,” he said. The MP also rejected the suggestion that he was avoiding lawful arrest by proceeding to Parliament after the incident. “This is an unlawful arrest. This is an unlawful arrest,” he said. He described the attempted arrest as “an attempt to abduct me by persons who don’t want to work with law.” Mr Baffour Awuah said seeking sanctuary at Parliament was therefore justified. “It is not wrong if I’m seeking sanctuary. It is not wrong if I’m seeking sanctuary,” he said. “In fact, you seek sanctuary against kidnappers, and so if I’m seeking sanctuary, it is not wrong.”

items.title: Indian election chief’s ouster sought after voter-roll revision probe
items.description: NEW DELHI: India’s political opposition dema­nded the removal of the top election official on Wednesday after a newspaper investigation alle­g­ed that decisions behind a contentious voter-roll revision may have been taken illegally. The Election Commis­sion of India (ECI) has been under scrutiny in rec­ent months over the nationwide revision that has struck millions of names from voter lists since last year. The ruling party says the revision aims to strike off fraudulently registered voters, but the opposition argues it is politically motivated and also targeting legitimate ones. The report by the Indian Express focused on internal divisions within the three-member ECI. It said the body’s chief, Gyanesh Kumar, overruled objections from the other two members at least 14 times during the past 10 months, leading to the removals of some 130 million voters. Such overrulings may be unlawful because the commission is supposed to work based on the consensus of at least two members, according to the report. The Congress accused Kumar of acting unilaterally at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP. “It was already known that things were not exactly well within the ECI,” Congress party spok­esman Pawan Khera said in a social media post. “But just how messy, dysfunctional and, frankly, disturbing things had become is (now) laid bare.” K. C. Venugopal, another sen­ior Congress party leader, demanded Kumar’s “immediate removal” and a Supreme Court-mon­itored investigation. Arvind Kejriwal of the opp­o­sition Aam Aadmi Party accused Kumar of “vote-rigging”. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

Pakistan in uncharted waters as ‘super El Nino’ multiplies threats
items.description: • 2027 most likely to become hottest year ever • El Nino may impact monsoon, bring droughts to southern provinces; can cause 451,000 extra deaths ISLAMABAD: With 2027 likely to become the hottest year due to the cumulative effects of global warming and El Nino, Pakistan is in uncharted waters, as this weather pattern could push the country toward food insecurity and extreme temperatures. According to the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) and climate scientists, a very strong El Nino increases the likelihood of significant shifts in temperature and rainfall patterns across the globe, including Pakistan, whose southern provinces can experience drought-like conditions. The global mean surface temperature has already increased by 1.4°C since the pre-industrial era, but this “super El Nino”, with its natural warming, could add 0.3°C to this number, pushing surface temperatures to 1.7°C above pre-industrial levels. The World Food Programme noted El Nino is set to sharply increase hunger, with 274 million people in 45 countries forecast to be acutely food insecure by 2027-end — 49 million more than today. World Health Organisation’s Teresa Zak­aria also branded it “a significant public health threat” and a “risk multiplier”. “The most severe impacts will be experienced while climate shocks intersect with weak hea­l­th systems, limited access to healthcare, food insecurity, displacement and humanitarian crisis,” she warned, urging immediate action. ‘Gigantic El Nino’ Dr Fahad Saeed, a leading climate scientist at Berlin-based Climate Analytics, compared the current ‘gigantic El Nino’ to the one in 1877-78, the “most severe on record”, that caused millions of deaths. “Such an intense event may impact the monsoon patterns and bring droughts, particularly in southern provinces,” said Dr Saeed. “But it is not clearly written on the horizon,” he said, pointing to multiple factors that can influence rainfall. The WMO said it may peak towards the end of the year, with scientists suggesting that its impact will last well into 2027. Dr Regina Rodrigues, professor of physical oceanography and climate at the Federal University of Santa Catarina in Brazil, said not every event is the same — they start, peak, and end at different times. She said they usually start around June-July and peak around December-February, but the current event is unusually strong, so it is difficult to pinpoint its peak or strength. “…What I expect for 2027 is that it will be the warmest year on record if El Nino continues as it generally does. The impact on several places is also harder in the second half — a lot of extreme events happen in the second half of El Nino,” she said. Pakistan has already received below-normal monsoon rainfall in June (19 per cent deficit), July (11pc), and August (23pc), according to the Pakistan Meteorological Department. This outlook was not surprising, because multiple studies point to increased monsoon rainfall variability and extremes. How El Nino will impact next year’s rainfall is uncertain at this point, but historical trends suggest South Asia experiences dry spells during such periods. Heat and droughts Dr Ali Mirchi and Dr Arfan Arshad, who authored an important study on 2022 floods, said rainfall during El Nino has not followed a “completely consistent pattern” in Pakistan. “Historically, El Nino has generally been associated with weaker summer monsoon rainfall, but it does not mean that every El Nino year is dry. A Pakistan Meteorological Department study examining rainfall from 1951 to 2012 found that eight out of 11 El Nino events were associated with below-normal monsoon rainfall. However, three El Nino years — 1977, 1994 and 1997 — experienced above-normal rainfall,” they said, adding that the data shows that El Nino increases the likelihood of a weaker monsoon, but it is “not a guarantee of drought”. For Dr Saeed, one of the major consequences of warmer temperatures driven by El Nino could be deadly heat waves in the southern districts of Pakistan. He referred to the deadly heat waves of 2015, 2016 and 2024 (all El Nino years), saying that most of the deaths due to heat in Pakistan were not counted. Over 1,000 people reportedly died in the 2015 heatwave. If heat conditions persisted, it could impact agriculture, said Dr Saeed. For instance, the country’s worst modern drought ran from 1999 to 2002, with agricultural output hit hardest in 2000-01 and significant migration out of Sindh and Balochistan. It followed the 1997-98 El Nino but coincided largely with La Nina conditions, which shows how indirectly ENSO (El Nino–Southern Oscillation) can translate into drought on the ground. Becoming frequent Dr Rodrigues noted that climate models show that strong El Nino events were becoming frequent. The period between two strong El Nino events used to be around 15 years (1982-83, 1997-98, 2015-16 events), but it was then reduced to nine years when we had the 2023-24 El Nino. “And now we are having another really strong El Nino, and it’s been only three years since. This is exactly what climate models forecast: increased frequency and stronger events,” she added. As scientists point to a possibility of an increase in such events, experts urged the government to take a proactive approach to deal with any eventuality arising out of these natural climate variations that can adversely imp­act agriculture through droughts and floods. 451,000 deaths This year’s El Nino weather pattern could lead to 451,000 additional heat-related deaths worldwide through February as it turbocharges global temperatures, according to projections published on Wednesday, according to AFP . The Sahel region in Africa could have an additional 66,800 heat deaths compared to a normal year, with nearly half of that number in Nigeria alone. An additional 19,300 are projected in Indonesia and 19,400 in the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, and Cambodia. The toll could reach 15,800 in India and 13,300 in Brazil. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

items.title: Cocobod pitches $1.4 billion domestic financing plan
items.description: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) is seeking to raise GH¢16.3 billion ($1.4 billion) from domestic investors to fund cocoa purchases for the upcoming season, according to a government presentation to investors. The national regulator is turning to domestic debt markets to fund its operations after struggling to finance ​the sector since its decade-old syndicated loan arrangement with international banks collapsed during the 2023/24 ​season. A separate arrangement under which international trading houses pre-financed purchases fell through last ⁠season, contributing to delays in payments to farmers. Farmers and buyers have blamed funding challenges for uncertainty over ​the timing of the new season. Cocoa Capital PLC, a new special purpose vehicle, is expected to issue ​a first tranche of debt to raise funds this week, comprising a 2.3 billion cedi bond and 4 billion cedi in commercial paper. Commercial paper with tenors of up to 270 days will be used to finance seasonal cocoa purchases, ​while bonds with a maturity of up to five years will be used to refinance existing short-term ​debts held by COCOBOD, according to the presentation made last Thursday. Ghana’s cocoa buyers last week said they were owed about ‌4 ⁠billion cedis by COCOBOD for last season’s crop, and want it paid before the new crop year begins. The Chamber of Cocoa Marketers, which represents the country’s licensed cocoa buyers, also warned that financing may not yet be in place to fund purchases once the season opens. NEW SEASON NOT YET STARTED Ghana ​and Ivory Coast, the world’s ​two biggest cocoa ⁠producers, agreed in June to harmonise their farmgate prices and season start dates, following a meeting between the two countries’ presidents. While Ivory Coast’s season opened on September 1, ​Ghana is yet to announce a start date. Debt repayments will be backed ​by assigned ⁠cocoa export receivables generated from selected forward sales contracts, the presentation showed. Eligible participants include commercial banks, pension funds, insurance companies, stockbrokers, high-net-worth individuals, other institutional investors and international cocoa buyers. COCOBOD did not respond to a request ⁠for ​comment on the new issuance. It said on X last week that ​the government had engaged investors, describing the planned issuance as a shift towards mobilising Ghana’s domestic capital market to finance the ​cocoa sector.

items.title: Saudi air strikes leave 10 dead, 14 injured in Yemen
items.description: DUBAI: Saudi airstrikes killed 10 people and wounded 14 others over the past 24 hours, Houthi-affiliated media reported on Wednesday, as the group warned they will attack US interests in the Middle East if Washington intervenes in the country’s conflict to support Saudi Arabia. The threat of regional escalation comes after Houthis staged a lightning offensive in recent weeks to gain control over Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait. A Houthi military adviser told AFP the group would strike American targets if the US attempts to unblock the narrow shipping lane. Houthis threaten to attack US interests if Washington supports Riyadh-led strikes “If America dares to intervene militarily with its fleets or tries to take control of Bab al-Mandab, it is a red line for them and anyone else … we will fight over it,” military adviser Abed Mohammed al-Thawr said. “If America gambles on supporting Saudi Arabia with airstrikes or air support … we will consider any American interests around us to be targets and we will not exclude anything,” he added. Thawr also noted the group would “close Bab al-Mandab completely to American ships” in the event of an intervention. The statements follow US reports that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Yemen’s government requested military assistance from US President Donald Trump. On the ground, violence continues to escalate. Al-Masirah TV reported on Wednesday that recent Saudi airstrikes resulted in dozens of casualties across two governorates. “Eight civilians were killed and 11 others wounded in Taiz, while two civilians were killed and three others wounded in Al-Jawf,” the channel said. The Houthis say Saudi Arabia has conducted hundreds of strikes in Yemen since a four-year truce collapsed in July. In retaliation, the Houthis have aimed drone and missile strikes at Saudi sites, targeting the capital, Riyadh. “As long as Saudi Arabia insists on and continues killing our country and striking our people, we will strike with an iron fist,” Thawr said. Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

Espace AES et dynamique touristique : Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger scellent une alliance stratégique au SITHO 2026
items.description: Le 22 septembre 2026, le Parc d’exposition du SIAO de Ouagadougou a ouvert ses portes à la 16e édition du Salon international du tourisme et de l’hôtellerie de Ouagadougou (SITHO). Placé sous le haut patronage du Premier ministre, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, agissant au nom du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, l'événement réunit les acteurs du secteur autour du financement des projets structurants. Mettant en lumière la région du Guiriko ainsi que le Mali et le Niger comme pays invités spéciaux, ce rendez-vous majeur ambitionne de construire une offre touristique sahélienne intégrée, compétitive et résiliente au sein de l'espace de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Au cœur des allées animées du Parc d'exposition du SIAO, la cérémonie d'ouverture de la 16e édition du SITHO a donné le ton des priorités économiques de la région. Déroulé sous le thème central « Financement des projets structurants : un levier pour le développement du tourisme », le salon entend franchir un palier décisif : convertir le potentiel patrimonial de l'Afrique de l'Ouest en emplois durables et en opportunités viables pour les populations. Dans son discours d'ouverture, le Chef du Gouvernement a martelé l'urgence d'une mobilisation financière adaptée. Qu'il s'agisse de l'aménagement des sites, des capacités d'hébergement, des réseaux de mobilité, des solutions numériques ou de la formation professionnelle, la compétition internationale exige des investissements conséquents. Le Premier ministre a ainsi exhorté les investisseurs, les collectivités et le secteur privé à multiplier les synergies pour faire émerger des projets bancables et durables. Cette 16e édition marque une étape politique et culturelle importante dans la consolidation de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Avec le Mali et le Niger mis à l'honneur comme pays invités spéciaux, le salon consacre une place centrale à la coopération régionale. La programmation du Forum des acteurs du tourisme de l’AES vise précisément à harmoniser les circuits, mutualiser les ressources et cofinancer des projets d'envergure. S'exprimant au nom des délégations invitées, le ministre malien de l'Artisanat, de la Culture, de l'Industrie Hôtelière et du Tourisme, Mamou DAFFÉ, a réaffirmé la volonté commune de promouvoir un espace touristique sahélien unifié. En s'appuyant sur la proximité géographique, les liens historiques et la richesse partagée de la gastronomie, de l'artisanat et des sites historiques, les pays membres entendent proposer une offre touristique complémentaire et souveraine. Au-delà de sa dimension purement économique, le tourisme a été réaffirmé comme un vecteur fondamental d'identité, de souveraineté et de cohésion sociale. « Le tourisme ne se limite pas à la découverte de paysages (…). Il est également un puissant vecteur de connaissance mutuelle et de valorisation de notre patrimoine », a rappelé le Premier ministre. Cette dynamique repose toutefois sur un préalable indispensable : la sécurité. À cet égard, un hommage appuyé a été rendu aux forces combattantes dont l'engagement sur le terrain garantit la protection du territoire, la libre circulation des visiteurs et la tenue de tels rassemblements d'envergure. La résilience des professionnels de l'hôtellerie et du tourisme, qui poursuivent leurs efforts d'innovation malgré les défis majeurs, a également été saluée. Rythmée par une prestation remarquable du Ballet national du Burkina Faso, la journée inaugurale s'est conclue par la visite officielle des stands par le Premier ministre et les autorités présentes. Jusqu'au 27 septembre, le parc du SIAO sera le théâtre d'expositions professionnelles, de rencontres B2B, d'espaces gastronomiques, de concours et d'excursions. En mettant la région du Guiriko à l'honneur, cette édition entend prouver que le Sahel reste une terre de culture, d'accueil et d'opportunités économiques majeures. L’article Espace AES et dynamique touristique : Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger scellent une alliance stratégique au SITHO 2026 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn Gaza recovery plan
items.description: flanked by Major General Jasper Jeffers of the US military (left) and Palestinian civil engineer Ali Shaath, Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza, speaks during a Board of Peace session.—AFP • 66 projects target housing and economic recovery over six months • Israeli fire kills two people in Gaza, officials say • UN chief warns time running out for two-state solution NEW YORK: US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace announced a $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan on Wednesday at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months. The presentation in New York coincided with the UN General Assembly, where world leaders like French Presi­dent Emmanuel Macron and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan took aim at the humanitarian situation in Gaza and called for action to end the conflict. The proposal involves 66 projects spanning over six months, covering temporary housing and efforts toward economic recovery. Trump is the chairman of the Board of Peace , which was initially designed to oversee a Gaza truce and the territory’s reconstruction following the war between Hamas and Israel. Nickolay Mladenov, the board’s high representative for Gaza, urged backing for the plan. Acknowledging that discussions with Israel are not easy ahead of the country’s elections, he noted conditions are politically sensitive. “Given the complexity of what we’re dealing with,” Mladenov said, progress is being made. Also present at Wednesday’s gathering were Trump’s roving envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Israeli killings Meanwhile, on the ground in Gaza, an Israeli airstrike hit a vehicle in western Khan Younis on Wednesday, killing two men and wounding two others, local health officials said. Medics identified the dead as Osama Abu Khater and Mohammad Abu Elwan. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement the military had killed Abu Elwan, describing him as a senior Hamas finance official. “We will not allow Hamas to rebuild its strength, and we will not stop until Hamas no longer exists in Gaza,” the statement said. Hamas did not immediately comment. Palestinian authorities say more than 73,000 people have been killed in Israel’s assault since Oct 7, 2023. UN figures show that by October 2025, Israeli strikes had left 84 per cent of all structures damaged or destroyed. A US-brokered ceasefire agreed to last year calls for eventual reconstruction, but little progress has been made. Negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops, and airstrikes have continued. Since the ceasefire took effect, at least 1,400 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed, according to territory health officials. The Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Israel and Hamas trade blame over responsibility for ceasefire violations. ‘Illegal expansion’ Separately, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres warned that the two-state solution for the Israel-Palestine conflict is at risk of collapse amid illegal Israeli settlement expansion and annexation. Speaking at a high-level meeting on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Guterres said actions on the ground in the Occupied Palestinian Territory are threatening progress. “The conditions for an independent, democratic, contiguous, viable and sovereign Palestinian state are being systematically erased,” he said, pointing to Israeli actions from war-ravaged Gaza to settler attacks in the West Bank. The meeting, titled “The Road Ahead”, examines the two-state solution and a comprehensive peace plan for Gaza. It builds on the September 2025 adoption of the New York Declaration to end the war that erupted in 2023, which has led to widespread destruction and more than 70,000 Palestinians killed. Guterres called for full implementation of US President Donald Trump’s 20-point provisional deal and the October 2025 ceasefire. He also urged an end to settlement expansion, prevention of annexation and support for Palestinian institutions. “There is simply no alternative,” he said, “and time is running out.” Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026

items.title: Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual consent
items.description: Christian Eriksen has left Wolfsburg by mutual consent, just over three months after collapsing during Denmark’s friendly with Ukraine. The former Manchester United midfielder’s contract with the German second-tier side was set to run until June 2027. Eriksen, 34, had previously suffered a cardiac arrest during Denmark’s opening European Championship group match against Finland in Copenhagen in 2021. “At the moment, it is important for me to be close to my family in Denmark. I’m pleased that we were able to find a solution together,” Eriksen said. “My time in Wolfsburg was marked by many highs and lows. I know that the club is now in good hands as it aims to make its way back to the Bundesliga, and I am convinced that a successful future lies ahead.” Eriksen, who has not played since June, joined Wolfsburg as a free agent a year ago after leaving Manchester United and made 34 appearances for the club. The 151-cap international has previously played for Ajax, Tottenham, Inter Milan and Brentford. In a statement, Wolfsburg’s managing director for sport, Dieter Hecking, said: “It was clear that the decision about his future had to be Christian’s. “We wanted to give him that freedom in this particular situation and have now agreed to his request to terminate the contract. “Despite his short time here, he has left a lasting impression on his team-mates, our staff and the fans.”

items.title: Meta frappe fort contre les réseaux d’escrocs : 3,7 millions de comptes et pages ciblés
items.description: Meta a annoncé la suppression ou la désactivation de 3,7 millions de comptes, pages et autres contenus liés à des escroqueries en ligne, grâce notamment aux informations transmises par la police de Singapour. Une coopération qui permet au géant américain de mieux identifier les réseaux de fraude opérant sur Facebook et Instagram. Entre janvier et juin 2026, Meta a supprimé plus de 113.000 entités et pages liées à la fraude sur Facebook et Instagram. En juillet, le groupe a également pris des mesures contre plus de 3,6 millions d’entités et de pages, dont une grande partie était constituée de comptes inactifs susceptibles d’être récupérés ultérieurement par des escrocs. Cette opération s'appuie notamment sur une collaboration engagée depuis deux ans avec les autorités singapouriennes. Selon Meta, le partage d'informations avec la police de Singapour a permis d'identifier non seulement des comptes isolés, mais de démanteler des réseaux entiers d'escrocs. Les fraudeurs utilisent aujourd'hui des méthodes de plus en plus sophistiquées. D'après Meta, l'intelligence artificielle leur permet notamment de créer rapidement de faux profils, de générer des images trompeuses ou encore de produire du code malveillant. Le groupe américain estime ainsi que la lutte contre les arnaques ne peut plus se limiter à la suppression de comptes individuels. L'objectif est désormais d'identifier les infrastructures et les réseaux qui permettent à ces activités frauduleuses de se développer à grande échelle. Cette stratégie intervient alors que les escroqueries en ligne touchent de nombreux secteurs, notamment les voyages, les investissements et les ventes sur internet. En juin seulement, Meta indique avoir pris des mesures contre plus de 33.600 entités et pages associées à des arnaques, notamment dans le domaine de la vente de voyages. items.title: Filing season ends
items.description: AS tax-filing season draws to a close, for those innocent enough to be part of the exercise, it is perhaps worth taking stock of what has worked and what has not in the recent past. One thing that has clearly not worked is schemes designed to give retailers incentives to become filers. Another thing that has not worked is mounting penalties on non-filers, and ramping up the FBR’s powers to enforce such schemes. Let me qualify what I said. When I say these have ‘not worked’ I mean something specific: they have not worked to break the barrier that keeps our tax-to-GDP ratio so dismally low that the structural fiscal deficit becomes the biggest ball and chain that holds the rest of the economy back. There is only one way to end this vicious cycle, and that is to come up with a tax reform programme that unlocks the significant tax potential locked up in those areas of the economy that see large-scale turnovers but contribute little to nothing by way of taxes. Not surprisingly, most of these areas are found inside the services sector, which accounts for more than 50 per cent of our GDP (in constant 2015 prices). And within services one constant headache has been wholesalers and retailers, second only in size to communications, whose size and weight are inflated due to the sheer scale of mobile communications in Pakistan. Mobile communications are reasonably easy for the tax machinery to reach. In his first year of power, Gen Pervez Musharraf targeted the retailers in a documentation drive, and the combined efforts of the FBR and the interior ministry, then headed by retired Gen Moinuddin Haider, were brought to bear on the problem. They used a raw power approach, demanding traders register themselves or face forcible closure of their business. And this ‘documentation drive’ faced its first big test in the sprawling Bara market of Peshawar, which was a major hub for undocumented frontier trade in those days. Yet again, the authorities are trying to incentivise retailers to self-register using yet another fixed tax scheme. It was the most dramatic showdown between the state and the retailers that we have probably ever seen. But eventually, the drive failed, and it turned out to be the last time the state ever used head-on collision as its strategy for bringing retailers into the net and documenting the economy. The priority lay dormant after that. Once the 9/11 bonanza got going, nobody was too pushed with the documentation drive or widening the tax net. The next time the matter was taken up was as part of the 2008 IMF programme, which had only one structural reform criterion: implement the value added tax. They called it Reformed GST, or RGST, at the time, to underline the fact that this was not a new tax but simply an upgraded version of something that had already been under implementation since 1991. The idea under this strategy was to incentivise traders, suppliers and vendors and distributors and wholesalers and all parties that were part of the supply chains connected with manufacturing in this country to help document each other. Every party would only pay tax on the portion of value that they added to a good. So they had to declare how much they bought an item for and from whom, and how much they sold it for and to whom, and pay tax only on the difference between these two prices. This also failed because the traders mounted enough of a protest against the tax for it to be defeated in parliament, mainly because the government’s own coalition partners opposed it. And after this defeat came a series of ad hoc attempts, organic, home-grown attempts, to try and net the retailers. The first of these was a combination of a set of penalties for the remaining non-compliant, coupled with an incentive to comply by declaring one’s assets and incomes via an amnesty scheme. This was in 2015. This was the first carrot-and-stick approach to this problem of rising undocumented incomes in the services sector. It sounded good at the time, especially since it was also coupled with large withholding taxes on bank transactions of non-filers of income tax returns. But these measures also failed. And then came yet more subtle measures. In 2017, they created a category called Tier 1 retailers, covering chain-store outlets, shops in air-conditioned malls, retailers with an annual electricity bill over Rs600,000, and wholesaler-cum-retailers. A little earlier, they had started using information from electricity bills to assess tax liability and make the collection. Much of the tax effort then focused on these Tier 1 retailers, expanding and contracting their definition over the years, adding and removing penalties, bringing in technology like point of sale (POS) machine integration, and running lottery schemes against the receipts issued through these machines. In 2022, they brought in a fixed tax of Rs3,000, 5,000 or 10,000, depending on the bill size, for non-Tier 1 retailers, to be collected through electricity bills. None of it worked. And now they tried, one more time, in the latest finance act, to incentivise retailers once again to self-register using yet another fixed tax scheme. According to a news report by Shahbaz Rana, “[o]nly two new traders have so far opted for the 1pc fixed tax scheme while another 315 shopkeepers who have filed returns are already part of the tax regime”. This strongly suggests that the latest version of the same scheme is now headed towards failure. It was easy to see this coming, given how all previous incentives and fixed tax schemes have fared in the past one decade. As the curtain prepares to drop on tax-filing season, it has become another ritual to observe the long and rather discouraging track record of the state’s failure to keep its fiscal effort up to date with the changes its economy has undergone over the years. And the innocent ones, like you and me, who file our taxes dutifully every year, pay the price. The writer is a business and economy journalist. khurram.husain@gmail.com X: @khurramhusain Published in Dawn, September 24th, 2026
